specs.ram: 16 to 32GB DDR5 (32GB recommended by forum members)

products.room_fit: Lives on a laptop tray, cart shelf, or wall shelf beside the bay; one HDMI run to the projector. Fold-away bays like it because it packs away with the mat.
products.who_its_for: The builder who wants one machine for the sim and the house, a garage bay that gets packed up, or lessons on the road.
pros: Forum members single out Legion cooling as the reason to pick it over other laptops
HDMI 2.1 plus USB-C DisplayPort handles a 4K60 projector
Lowest-cost current laptop that clears the 12GB VRAM 4K threshold (Pro 5i)
cons: Laptop GPU of the same name is 20 to 30 percent slower than the desktop card
Cannot upgrade the GPU later
Loud under sustained load (Pro 7i)
known_issues: Must force the discrete GPU via MUX or dGPU-only mode or GSPro can land on integrated graphics at single-digit fps
Thin chassis throttle after 20 to 30 minutes; members report burnt-out gaming laptops running GSPro and FSX Play
Battery drains in a few holes if unplugged; keep it on the charger and cap charge around 80 percent
products.why_people_choose_it: It is the laptop forum regulars name first when someone asks, because the cooling holds up through a full round and the RTX 4060 or 5060 trim sits right on GSPro's official 1080p laptop line.

products.room_fit: A mid tower; owners show it in a PC cabinet behind the golfer or on a low shelf. Too tall for a cart tray; fine on a cart base.
products.who_its_for: The buyer who wants the PC to arrive with GSPro or FSX installed and activated, with golf-specific support and a 2-year warranty, and is willing to pay roughly $600 to $1,000 over an equivalent Amazon tower for it.
pros: Software preinstalled and activated, setup help included
Two powered USB ports and a camera-card slot for swing cameras
Two Ethernet ports out of the box (one for a wired launch monitor, one for internet)
cons: Price premium over a comparable iBUYPOWER or CyberPowerPC tower
Only one free expansion slot: the GPU blocks the rest, so a camera card and an extra NIC cannot both go in without a riser
Core Ultra 5 in the 5702 and 5702Ti sits below E6 (2026)'s i7 10th gen+ line and below Trackman/Uneekor's i7 lists
known_issues: SG3-5602 shows out of stock on surfthing.com (2026-10-19)
Most reviews come from retailers or affiliate sites; the Golf Simulator Videos review is affiliate-linked
products.why_people_choose_it: Forum members who bought one say they paid about $3,300 all-in and 'could have done it for less', but got the courses loaded and someone to call. It is the turnkey answer for people who do not want to spec a PC.

blog_outline.title: The computer is the last thing you buy and the first thing you should decide: PCs, laptops and the no-PC path for a garage golf simulator (2026)
sections: The software decides the PC: a one-table map of GSPro (RTX 3060 / 16GB at 1080p, RTX 3080 or 4070 / 32GB at 4K, Windows only), E6 Connect (GTX 1070 / 8GB, also iPad), E6 (2026) (RTX 3060 12GB / 24GB / i7, PC only), Foresight Premier (RTX 3060 Ti class minimum, replaces FSX Play), TGC 2019 (GTX 1060 class), Creative Golf 3D, and Awesome Golf (integrated graphics, iPad). Pick the heaviest title you will run at your projector's resolution, then buy one tier up.

1080p or 4K is the real fork: most garage bays run a 1080p projector, and a GolfWRX regular says there is hardly any difference in GSPro without a very good projector. 1080p means an RTX 4060 / 5060 desktop or an RTX 4060 laptop; 4K means 12GB of VRAM and 32GB of RAM and roughly doubles the budget.

The gaming-laptop path and its limits: GSPro's own laptop table (RTX 4060 Laptop for 1080p, 4070 for 1080p Ultra, 4080 for 4K), why a laptop card is 20 to 30 percent slower than the desktop card of the same name, MUX and dGPU-only mode, thin-chassis throttling after 20 to 30 minutes, the cooling pad, the 80 percent charge cap, and the burnt-out laptops in the forum. The models that keep coming up: Lenovo Legion 5i / Pro 5i, ASUS TUF and ROG Strix, Dell G15 (now Alienware 15), MSI Thin 15 and Katana, Acer Nitro V. Brett's own older gaming laptop as the worked example.

Prebuilts under $1,000 (as of the read date): a refurbished office tower plus a used RTX 3060, Amazon house-brand RTX 4060 towers (ViprTech, STGAubron, MXZ) at $800 to $950, and the Costco RTX 4060 tower that forum members call the best deal going. What to check: power supply, one free PCIe slot, an Ethernet port if the launch monitor is wired.

Prebuilts under $1,500: iBUYPOWER Slate Mesh, Skytech Azure 3, MSI Codex R2, Lenovo Legion Tower 5i; RTX 5060 / 5060 Ti class, 32GB if you can; the HP Omen 35L and Alienware 16 laptops from big-box stores.

Prebuilts under $2,500 and the turnkey option: iBUYPOWER Element RTX 5070, CyberPowerPC Master 8000 / 9000, Alienware Aurora from $2,329.99, and SurfThing SG3-5602 ($2,249) / SG3-5702 ($3,199) with the software preinstalled, two Ethernet ports and camera-powered USB. When the premium is worth it (you want someone to call) and when it is not (you can plug in a GPU).

Mini PCs: Beelink SER8 and Minisforum UM890 Pro (780M) run Awesome Golf, SkyTrak and E6 but sit under every GSPro floor; the Minisforum AtomMan G1 Pro puts a desktop RTX 5060 in a cart-shelf box at $1,719; handhelds (Legion Go, ROG Ally) are a curiosity.

The no-PC path: Garmin R10 ($499 to $599) or Mevo+ ($1,099 clearance) or Rapsodo MLM2PRO ($549.99) to an iPad, then Apple TV AirPlay or a $20 HDMI adapter to the projector. What you get (E6 iOS courses, Awesome Golf, FS Golf, Home Tee Hero), what you give up (GSPro, TGC, Premier, 4:3 output, older-iPad stutter), and the hidden costs (Garmin $99/yr, Rapsodo Premium $199.99/yr, E6 and Awesome Golf subscriptions).

What to put on a cart in a fold-away bay: a laptop or a mini tower on a two-shelf AV cart with the projector on top, one 25 ft HDMI 2.1 run, a USB Ethernet adapter for a wired launch monitor, a small UPS, and the PC off the carpet with its vents clear. Keep the tower out of a closed cabinet, keep the laptop on the charger, and dust the fans monthly.

Checklist before you click buy: Windows 11, the GPU on the right tier for your software and resolution, 32GB RAM if 4K or cameras, 1TB NVMe (courses are 1 to 5GB each), two Ethernet ports or a spare slot if wired, HDMI 2.1 or USB-C DisplayPort for 4K60, and a return policy.
